# ms: # hermes 0.17.0, captured 2026-09-04 in a Sidecar-managed shell on a private
# tmux server, with HERMES_HOME, XDG_STATE_HOME and -config all under a scratch
# tree. One non-interactive turn: `hermes -z "reply with the single word ok"`.
# HOW IT WAS CAPTURED. A probe plugin registering every name in Hermes's
# VALID_HOOKS ran beside Sidecar's own asset and recorded, per invocation, the
# hook name, the platform, whether a session id was present, and the payload's
# field NAMES. The shipped asset subscribes to three of these; the rest are here
# because what a provider DOES fire is the evidence behind every gap the
# capability entry claims, and reading the call sites alone had got two of them
# wrong.
# THREE FINDINGS.
# 1. on_session_start fires BEFORE the first model call, carrying platform and
# session_id. That is the earliest binding any provider in this catalog offers:
# grok's SessionStart and Antigravity's PreInvocation both arrive one turn into a
# pane's life. Reading hermes_cli/plugins.py's call sites suggested the opposite
# -- no invoke_hook("on_session_start") is greppable in the tree -- which is
# exactly why this was measured.
# 2. on_session_start and pre_llm_call arrive half a second apart with the SAME
# session id. Upstream's asset reports the binding on both; Sidecar's suppresses
# the repeat, because each report here is a process spawn taking a file lock.
# 3. Every payload in a terminal session carries platform=cli, and the field is
# what the interactive-platform gate reads. pre_tool_call and post_tool_call did
# not fire in this turn (nothing used a tool) and carry no platform kwarg at all
# at their call sites in model_tools.py, which is why the asset's gate refuses
# them even though they carry a session id.
# NOT CAPTURED: on_session_reset, which needs an interactive TUI and /new. Its
# call site in cli.py passes session_id, platform and reason, and the asset
# treats it exactly as it treats a start.
# The binding this run produced was corroborated from Hermes's own side:
# `hermes sessions list` printed the same session id Sidecar had recorded.
